jobs.title: Associate Vice President, Strategy
jobs.excerpt: HighlightsThis is an Associate Vice President-level leadership role for the Strategy discipline.
jobs.description:
Highlights

This is an Associate Vice President-level leadership role for the Strategy discipline. We are looking for someone with at least 10 years of experience leading strategy engagements that include research, analysis, insight development, and strategic direction. Experience within a brand or creative agency environment is strongly preferred, along with demonstrated success developing strategists, evolving methodologies, and guiding complex Partner engagements.

At Parisleaf, we expect someone in this role to:

  • Lead the Strategy discipline, establishing clear standards, methodologies, and best practices that strengthen the quality and consistency of our work.
  • Provide strategic oversight across engagements, ensuring insights are meaningful, recommendations are actionable, and deliverables support each Partner’s goals.
  • Coach, develop, and manage Strategy team members, providing the clarity, feedback, and support they need to grow and deliver excellent work.
  • Serve as a trusted senior advisor and lead facilitator in Partner interactions, navigating complex stakeholders and guiding teams toward alignment and confident decisions.
  • Collaborate with leaders across disciplines to strengthen integrated delivery, proactively identify risks, and ensure strategy effectively informs creative outcomes.
  • Contribute to company growth by supporting business development, identifying opportunities to expand Partner relationships, and advancing company-wide priorities.

About Parisleaf

We are a brand & digital agency specializing in partnering with Nonprofits. Most of our work helps support fundraising efforts by building brands for major fundraising campaigns. As we often say, money is mission fuel in the right hands.

We’re seeking people who share our values of gratitude, responsibility, integrity, candor, and empathy. Curious people who believe good strategy and good design can drive fundraising. We love making things for a living and are in it for the long haul. For us at Parisleaf, that means designing an agency culture built on love and grounded in integrity. Whether the role is in creative, operations, or business development, everyone at Parisleaf is dedicated to helping partners (or Partners, as we refer to them) find and show their purpose.

Our partners want to leave their corner of the world a little better than they found it. They seek creative partners who will advocate for their audience. They want substance and style. They hire us for who we are as much or more than what we do.

About You

You are a strategic leader who thrives at the intersection of people, ideas, and impact. Equal parts coach, practitioner, and partner, you’ll lead our Strategy discipline while continuing to guide some of our most important partner engagements. You’re energized by developing others just as much as you are by solving complex strategic challenges, and you find fulfillment in helping both teammates and partners grow.

You believe great strategy isn’t just about delivering recommendations—it’s about creating clarity, building alignment, and empowering organizations to move confidently toward their vision. You’re comfortable leading executive-level conversations, facilitating workshops with diverse stakeholders, and navigating ambiguity with confidence and empathy. You know how to ask the questions others haven’t considered, uncover meaningful insights, and guide teams toward thoughtful, actionable solutions.

You have a deep appreciation for branding and the many ways it comes to life—from messaging and visual identity to digital experiences, campaigns, and activation. You think holistically, ensuring strategic insights translate into work that is both creatively compelling and organizationally meaningful.

You’re an exceptional relationship builder. You earn trust quickly, cultivate long-term partnerships, and naturally identify opportunities to deepen relationships over time. While traditional sales may not be your passion, you’re energized by stewarding partner relationships, supporting renewals, identifying opportunities for expanded engagement, and helping prospective partners understand the value Parisleaf can bring to their mission.

As a leader, you love helping others succeed. You enjoy coaching strategists, elevating the quality of their thinking, and creating the systems, methodologies, and feedback that strengthen an entire discipline. You’re excited to shape how strategy is practiced at Parisleaf—not just by doing exceptional work yourself, but by building a team capable of delivering it consistently.

You are curious, organized, proactive, and deeply collaborative. You create clarity from complexity, communicate with confidence and humility, and know when to lead, when to listen, and when to challenge assumptions. You think on your feet, read the room well, and bring both rigor and warmth to every interaction. You can confidently defend your recommendations with wisdom, research, and sound judgment, while always setting your ego aside in service of the best outcome for our partners and teammates.

Your experience in the nonprofit and fundraising sector is highly valued. You understand the unique opportunities and challenges mission-driven organizations face and are passionate about helping them build brands and campaigns that inspire generosity and advance their missions.

The Role

The Associate Vice President of Strategy is responsible for leading and developing the Strategy discipline at Parisleaf. This role oversees the quality, consistency, and evolution of our strategic work while managing and mentoring the Strategy team. As a senior strategic leader, the Associate Vice President serves as a trusted advisor to partners, guides complex engagements, and helps shape the agency’s strategic point of view.

The Associate Vice President of Strategy works closely with Creative, Operations, Business Development, and Leadership to ensure strategic excellence across all partner engagements and to continuously strengthen Parisleaf's methodologies, processes, and offerings.

Team Leadership & Development

  • Directly manage, coach, and develop members of the Strategy team.
  • Conduct regular one-on-ones, performance reviews, development planning, and internal meetings, as appropriate. .
  • Establish clear expectations and accountability for strategic excellence.
  • Support hiring, onboarding, and career pathing for Strategy team members.
  • Foster a culture of curiosity, collaboration, candor, and continuous learning.
  • Identify growth opportunities and help team members expand their skills and strategic capabilities.
  • Serve as the primary leader and advocate for the Strategy discipline within the agency.

Strategy Methodology & Process

  • Own and evolve Parisleaf's strategic methodologies, frameworks, tools, and best practices.
  • Ensure strategic processes are documented, scalable, and consistently applied across engagements.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of strategic work, especially within existing and emerging service lines.
  • Develop training, resources, and guidance that elevate the capabilities of the Strategy team and agency.
  • Partner with the Leadership Team to continuously refine how strategy integrates into the broader partner experience.
  • Help shape and improve agency offerings, services, and strategic deliverables.

Strategic Oversight

  • Maintain quality standards and strategic consistency across the agency’s portfolio of work.
  • Serve as a senior reviewer for key strategic recommendations, presentations, and deliverables.
  • Provide guidance and support to strategists navigating complex partner situations or strategic challenges.
  • Ensure strategic recommendations align with partner goals, fundraising objectives, organizational realities, and agency standards.
  • Identify emerging trends, opportunities, and innovations that strengthen Parisleaf's strategic offerings.
  • Ensure strategic recommendations are grounded in research, informed by stakeholder insights, and aligned with partner goals.
  • Help teams identify opportunities, risks, and areas requiring deeper strategic exploration.
  • Maintain a high standard of thinking, problem-solving, facilitation, and storytelling across all strategic work.
  • Ensure strategic insights are effectively translated into compelling creative and activation outcomes.

Partner Delivery

  • Maintain a pulse on all Partner accounts, providing strategic oversight, identifying risks and opportunities, and supporting teams when senior-level guidance is needed.
  • Lead complex, high-profile engagements from discovery through activation.
  • Serve as a senior advisor to Partner leadership teams, helping navigate organizational challenges, stakeholder dynamics, and critical decisions.
  • Facilitate executive-level workshops, strategic planning sessions, and alignment conversations.
  • Ensure strategic thinking remains consistent, actionable, and effective throughout every phase of an engagement.
  • Partner with Creative and Operations leaders to align strategic direction, execution, and Partner experience.
  • Guide recommendations across positioning, messaging, naming, campaign strategy, donor engagement, and activation.
  • Identify opportunities to deepen relationships, create additional value, and maintain momentum as Partner priorities evolve.

Business Development

  • Partner with Leadership and Business Development teams to pursue new partnership opportunities.
  • Participate in discovery conversations, proposal development, and partner pitches.
  • Contribute strategic thinking and fundraising expertise throughout the sales process.
  • Help shape solutions that align partner needs with Parisleaf's capabilities and approach.
  • Support the development of case studies, presentations, and strategic narratives that demonstrate agency impact.
  • Build relationships that contribute to agency growth and long-term partner success.

Agency Leadership

  • Serve as a leader within the agency, helping shape priorities, initiatives, and culture.
  • Contribute to annual planning, departmental goal setting, and strategic initiatives.
  • Champion strategic thinking across all departments and areas of the business.
  • Partner with Leadership to identify opportunities for agency growth, innovation, and improvement.
  • Contribute to thought leadership through speaking, writing, training, and knowledge sharing.
  • Support cross-functional collaboration and alignment across teams.
  • Act as a steward of Parisleaf's values, standards, and commitment to excellence.

Professional Expectations

  • Demonstrate exceptional communication skills in both written and verbal formats.
  • Exercise sound judgment and decision-making in complex situations.
  • Balance strategic thinking with practical execution and partner needs.
  • Effectively manage time, priorities, budgets, and scope across multiple engagements.
  • Build trust with partners, teammates, and stakeholders through integrity, candor, empathy, and accountability.
  • Remain curious, adaptable, and committed to continuous learning and improvement.

This is a full-time, remote, salaried position commensurate with experience. We are a fully distributed team. Travel is required.

The Opportunity

At Parisleaf, we write and design all kinds of things, but they always revolve around the brand. And we’re on a mission to help our partners fundraise to help fuel their mission. You will work with our multidisciplinary team on projects ranging from competitive analysis and stakeholder interviews to verbal and visual identity. You’ll devise strategies to ignite, support, and guide the team to build campaign brands, brand guides, print collateral, web, video, and environmental design.

You’ll spend a lot of time on Zoom and onsite with our partners. And while you’ll spend a lot of your time conducting and synthesizing research and developing a strategy for partners, you’ll also be responsible for helping us grow. We are looking for someone who enjoys developing ideas with partners and colleagues and can then hunker down and truly communicate and sell the power of that strategy.

While this is a new role at Parisleaf, we’ve been doing it all along. We’ve developed a proven research process, but we’re looking for someone who lives and breathes strategy and can make their mark on our work and help us continue to refine this department.

Background/Requirements

This is a full-time, remote salaried position commensurate with experience. We are a fully distributed team. Travel is required. We only accept applications from candidates currently residing in the continental United States. We are committed to building a diverse and passionate team. Women, people of color, and LGBTQ+ individuals are encouraged to apply.

Parisleaf provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, genetics, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or veteran status. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Salary: $140,000 – $160,000 / year

The SE plays a critical role in driving the technical sales process and enabling the success of our MSP ecosystem across the EMEA region. You will support both pre-sales engagements and partner enablement initiatives, helping MSPs onboard, deploy, and operationalize Absolute Security’s Secure Endpoint and Secure Access solutions within their managed offerings. As a technical evangelist for the Absolute platform, you represent the company in front of customers, partners, and at industry events—demonstrating our unique ability to deliver visibility, control, and resilience across complex environments.

You are adept at performing detailed technical discovery that uncovers the customer or partner’s current environment, identifies business risks and desired outcomes, and positions Absolute’s solutions to deliver measurable value. You can design and execute Proof of Value (PoV) engagements, tailor technical demonstrations, and help our partners validate and scale their managed service offerings.

In addition to customer-facing sales activities, you will collaborate with the CAM and the Partner Enablement team to lead MSP onboarding, technical training, and certification efforts—ensuring new partners are fully enabled to deliver Absolute-powered services to their end customers.
You thrive in a fast-paced environment, balancing technical depth with business impact, and can work independently while aligning closely with AEsa, CAMs, and Partner Success teams.

What You’ll Do

  • Stay current on emerging technologies, competitive positioning, and regulatory trends relevant to MSPs and enterprise cybersecurity

What You’ll Bring

  • Proven experience in sales engineering or solution architecture, ideally in cybersecurity, endpoint management, or secure access technologies
  • Strong technical background in security, networking, operating systems, and cloud infrastructure
  • Experience working with or within MSPs, with a clear understanding of service delivery models and recurring revenue motions.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, capable of influencing both technical and business audiences
  • Ability to thrive in a matrixed environment across sales, channel, and technical functions.
  • Proficiency in English; additional European languages (e.g., French, German, Spanish) are a strong advantage
  • Understanding of AV, EDR, Incident Response, Forensics, or other endpoint or network security tools
  • Familiar with popular firewall vendors and basic rule design
  • Familiar with endpoint security and patch management policies
  • Strong understanding of Windows (Desktop and Server), macOS, and Linux operating systems, including network stacks
  • Can troubleshoot complex network environments to support evaluations on customers’ premises or with the Absolute cloud hosted products
  • Experience with complex technical sales cycles, including deep discovery as well as scoping, executing, and presenting complex PoVs (evaluations)
  • Ability to communicate technical concepts to all levels of people, from IT, Network and Security managers to Line of Business owners to CIO and CISOs
  • Understanding of data-in-transit security, including TLS, IPsec, VPNs, PKI, and certificate management
  • Understanding of network services and systems including routing and local and wide area network design Familiar with popular firewall vendors and basic rule design
  • Understanding of authentication methods and protocols including SAML and RADIUS

Nice to Have skills

  • Experience selling SASE, SSE, VPN, EDR, Incident Response or other endpoint or network security tools
  • Experience with programming or scripting languages such as PowerShell, Python, or Bash
  • Experience with Cloud IaaS vendors including networking and security service operation
  • Security (CISSP, GIAC, CompTIA Security+, etc.) or networking (CCNA, CompTIA Network+, etc.) certifications
  • Experience in IT or Security operations

Why Work For Us
You’re resilient and passionate about securing the Work from Anywhere era. So are we.
We’re in search of the best and the brightest – everyone from innovators, sellers and marketers to financers, operators and especially customer relationship managers – we’re looking for top tier talent to help us shape the next decade of security, drive innovation that enables customers with truly disruptive solutions and are dedicated to making a meaningful difference.
Headquartered in Seattle, Washington with international offices in Vancouver - BC, Austin - TX, Boulder - CO, Ankeny – IA, Reading - UK and Ho Chi Minh City – Vietnam, Absolute Security accelerates customers’ shift to work-from-anywhere through the industry’s first self-healing Zero Trust platform, ensuring maximum security and uncompromised productivity. Only Absolute is embedded in more than half a billion devices, offering a permanent digital connection that intelligently and dynamically applies visibility, control and self-healing capabilities to endpoints, applications, and network access to ensure their cyber resilience tailored for distributed workforces.
Our vision is to be the world’s most trusted security company – and to empower end users to connect securely and from anywhere, to all the applications they need to collaborate and get their work done, without interruptions and with an optimal network experience. Absolute currently serves approximately 16,000 customers with more than 13 million activated endpoints globally. G2 recognized Absolute as a Leader in the Winter 2022 Endpoint Management and Zero Trust Networking Grid Reports, reflecting our continued customer satisfaction across product lines. To learn more about Absolute, visit our website at www.absolute.com or visit our YouTube channel

What you'll do

jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityAs a Market Curation Editor for Sports, you'll support the Product Data Operations team supporting a new social-predictions app moving through a beta launch.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

As a Market Curation Editor for Sports, you'll support the Product Data Operations team supporting a new social-predictions app moving through a beta launch. An automated pipeline drafts candidate prediction markets every night; you are the human judgment layer on top of it — deciding which go live, sharpening the ones that are nearly right, and catching the markets the pipeline missed entirely. This role calls for deep, current expertise in professional and collegiate sport and in the rule conventions that govern how results are officially determined.

What You'll Do

  • Review a daily queue of system-generated sports markets against a fixed completion deadline, working event by event across every market a fixture generates.
  • Assess each candidate market for factual accuracy, clarity, and whether the resolution criteria can actually be adjudicated against a named authoritative source and a defined settlement date.
  • Verify that open and close timing is correct for the underlying event, including scheduled and unscheduled delays.
  • Apply the correct settlement convention for the league in question — overtime, shootouts, postponement and abandonment, minimum-play thresholds on player props, and official statistical corrections.
  • Confirm policy fit against community standards and content guidelines, escalating anything ambiguous or sensitive rather than making an unsupported call.
  • Approve, edit, or reject each candidate, recording a structured reason every time — this record is a product deliverable, not admin.
  • Rewrite questions and resolution language for precision, and for how fans actually talk about the event.
  • Author timestamped clarifications when ambiguity emerges in a live market, and resolve settlement exceptions the data feed can't handle.
  • Run proactive gap scans — monitor live markets for visible errors, and track schedules, team news, and social platforms for events the pipeline didn't capture.
  • Participate in weekly calibration reviews to stay consistent with published guidelines and fellow curators.

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years in sports trading, sports data operations, sports journalism or editorial, or a comparable role requiring current subject-matter expertise.
  • Demonstrable current fluency in sport — following it now, not historically — across professional and collegiate leagues in major sports.
  • Fluency with sports culture and sports social media (trades, free agency, breaking news accounts).
  • Working knowledge of official rule and settlement conventions for major leagues, and of which sources are authoritative for results and statistics.
  • Proven judgment on edge cases: suspended and abandoned events, statistical corrections, contested outcomes, ambiguous official rulings.
  • Ability to interpret official sources quickly and reach a defensible determination.
  • Exceptional written precision under deadline — able to write unambiguous rules that hold up after the outcome is known.
  • Comfort applying a written policy framework, with the instinct to escalate rather than guess.
  • Flexible availability for evening, overnight, and weekend work as needed around live events.

Nice to Have

  • Experience trading on, or working with, prediction markets, sportsbooks, exchanges, or DFS platforms.
  • Prior work on a trading desk, or standing as a super-user of prediction apps.
  • Sports journalism background and/or experience contributing to guidelines, style guides, rulebooks, or annotation standards.
  • Familiarity with content policy, moderation frameworks, or editorial standards.

How We'll Measure Success

  • Consistent completion of the daily queue against the hard deadline.
  • Decision quality — agreement with peers and the lead on calibration samples, and a low rate of published markets requiring void, amendment, or resettlement.
  • Reason quality — structured rejection reasons that are specific and correctly categorized.
  • Rewrite quality — published questions that survive contact with the outcome without dispute.
  • Proactive contribution — relevant events and markets you surface that the pipeline didn't generate.

As a contractor you’ll supply a securecomputer and high‑speed internet; company‑sponsored benefits such as health insurance and PTO do not apply.

As Executive & Strategic Recruiter, you will own end-to-end search strategy and execution, partnering directly with hiring executives to define roles, map talent, and close candidates who weren't looking.

jobs.description:
Common Sense Privacy is defining the standard for privacy and trust in software. Our software provides independent privacy evaluation for companies that handle sensitive user data. We help businesses keep up with fast evolving regulations, customer expectations, and implement best practices. As global regulations and customer expectations evolve at breakneck speed, we empower businesses to not only stay compliant but to lead with best practices.
Companies who pass our rigorous assessment can apply for the privacy seal. The Common Sense Privacy Seal has become the credential that matters: the mark that tells buyers a company has been thoroughly evaluated and meets the highest privacy standards.
We're backed by Andrew Ng's AI Fund and built on the 20-year trusted foundation of Common Sense Media.
We've moved beyond early traction. We have revenue, and paying enterprise customers. We started in educational technology and are now expanding into additional verticals where privacy differentiation creates competitive advantage.

The Role

You’ll sell our privacy evaluation services—helping companies earn our seal and demonstrate credible privacy practices to their customers. Your job is simple: find companies who understand the importance of customer trust, show them how our seal differentiates them, and close contracts.
This is a full-cycle sales role. You’ll prospect, qualify, demo, negotiate, and close—working with warm inbound leads and identifying your own targets. You’ll carry quota and be measured on revenue.
Initially, you’ll focus on our established education technology market while exploring adjacent verticals. As you identify promising opportunities in new markets, you’ll test and validate them.

What You’ll Do Day-to-Day

You’ll spend your time on calls. Prospecting calls with companies that need credible privacy differentiation. Discovery calls understanding how our seal helps them compete. Demo calls walking through our evaluation process and what earning our seal means. Negotiation calls working through contract terms. You’ll update the CRM, forecast your pipeline, and collaborate with marketing on target account campaigns.
You’ll travel occasionally (15-20%) to attend conferences where you can meet prospects face-to-face—not just edtech events, but also healthcare IT, fintech, and HR tech conferences as we establish our standard in new markets.
This role reports directly to the CEO with responsibilities in the following areas:

Pipeline Generation (40%)

  • Work warm inbound leads from companies requesting to be evaluated for our seal
  • Identify and prospect target accounts: companies in education, healthcare SaaS, fintech, HR tech, or other verticals where our trust standard creates value
  • Use intent signals: companies responding to RFPs with privacy requirements, recently funded companies entering regulated markets, vendors facing buyer questions about trust and privacy
  • Leverage demand generation: when buyers ask vendors “how can we trust your privacy practices?”, you help those vendors earn our seal
  • Conduct outreach via email, LinkedIn, phone, and conference connections
  • Run discovery calls to qualify fit and understand how our seal helps them win deals

Deal Management (50%)

  • Run demos showing our evaluation process and what companies receive when they earn our seal
  • Navigate multiple stakeholders: product, legal, compliance, marketing, sales leadership
  • Position our seal as competitive differentiation: show how it helps companies win deals and build trust with privacy-conscious buyers
  • Handle objections around timing, cost, and ROI
  • Structure deals: seal evaluations, ongoing monitoring,, multi-product assessments
  • Coordinate with delivery team on evaluation timelines and seal issuance
  • Show ROI: our seal helps companies win competitive deals by proving their privacy practices

Market Development (10%)

  • Refine positioning of our seal and trust standard in new verticals beyond education
  • Identify patterns: which industries value our credential most, what triggers buying decisions
  • Share insights with leadership about market opportunities
  • Help refine how we position our seal for different buyer personas

Requirements For the Role Include:

  • 5+ years full-cycle B2B SaaS sales experience
  • Track record consistently hitting or exceeding quota ($750K-$ annually)
  • Experience selling deals in the $25K-$100K range
  • Experience selling across multiple industries—you can adapt your pitch for different markets
  • Proficiency with Salesforce (or similar CRM) and sales engagement tools
  • Strong discovery skills: can uncover pain, understand buying process, identify decision-makers
  • Effective demo and presentation skills
  • Ability to position credentials, certifications, or trust signals as competitive advantage
  • Self-motivated and disciplined in managing your own pipeline

Nice To Haves Include:

  • Experience selling privacy, compliance, security, or trust/safety solutions
  • Experience selling certification, assessment, or credential programs
  • Background selling to regulated industries (healthcare, finance, education)
  • Familiarity with enterprise procurement processes
  • Experience in early-stage or growth-stage startups where you helped develop new markets
  • Comfort with market ambiguity—you can test new approaches without perfect clarity

Compensation & Benefits

Common Sense Privacy offers a competitive compensation, equity and benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan, and flexible PTO

What Makes This Role Different

You’re selling something buyers actually want to see: credible proof that a company takes privacy seriously. Our seal matters because it’s backed by Common Sense Media’s 20-year reputation and rigorous independent evaluation.
When companies earn our seal, they can prove their privacy practices to skeptical buyers. When buyers see our seal, they know it means something. You’re not just selling software—you’re helping companies earn a credential that builds trust.
You’ll have the opportunity to shape which markets we pursue. You’ll help define our expansion strategy. You’re not just executing someone else’s plan—you’re discovering where our trust standard creates the most value.
The seal is real. The initial market is proven. Your job is to execute in education while building our next growth markets.
If you’re a closer who wants to sell something meaningful and help define a new standard, let’s talk.

We're seeking a Director to lead Deal Desk within Liftoff's Strategic Finance team that reports to the VP of Strategic Finance. This is a high-ownership role at the center of how Liftoff structures, approves, and manages commercial agreements, from standard arrangements to complex, non-standard deals with strategic advertising partners. As the ultimate DRI for revenue adjustments, deal economics, and the integrity of Liftoff's commercial commitments, you will partner closely with GTM, Finance, and senior leadership to set deal strategy, manage active deal performance, and ensure every commercial arrangement is entered into with a clear, defensible financial rationale. jobs.excerpt: Our client, a fast-growing eCommerce company in the Health Care space is seeking a commercially minded Creative Director to lead the creative function across our ecommerce business.
jobs.description:
Our client, a fast-growing eCommerce company in the Health Care space is seeking a commercially minded Creative Director to lead the creative function across our ecommerce business.

This role will own the complete creative direction of the brand across paid advertising, website and landing pages, email, organic social media, marketplaces, product launches, and other customer-facing channels.

The Creative Director will be responsible not only for maintaining a strong and consistent brand identity, but also for improving commercial performance. The primary objective of the role is to develop creative strategies and assets that increase conversion rates, improve advertising performance, strengthen customer engagement, and support profitable growth.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can combine creative judgement, customer insight, performance data, and strong team management.

Key Outcomes

Improve Ecommerce Conversion Performance

  • Develop creative strategies that improve conversion across paid media, websites, product pages, marketplaces, and email.
  • Turn customer insights, performance data, and competitor research into clear briefs and testable concepts.
  • Partner with ecommerce teams to improve client acquisition and conversion.
  • Establish a structured process for creative testing and optimisation.

Lead Performance Creative Strategy

  • Own creative strategy across paid social, video, display, and other acquisition channels.
  • Build a consistent pipeline of concepts, hooks, angles, scripts, and formats.
  • Ensure sufficient creative volume and variation for testing and scaling.
  • Use performance data to identify, improve, and scale winning concepts.
  • Balance direct-response effectiveness with strong brand presentation.

Strengthen Website and Product Pages Creatives

  • Lead creative direction across the website, landing pages, collection pages, and product pages.
  • Improve how product benefits, differentiation, use cases, and customer proof are communicated.
  • Create clear visual and messaging hierarchies that make pages more persuasive.
  • Collaborate with ecommerce, UX, development, copywriting, and CRO teams on improvements and testing.
  • Ensure consistency between advertising and onsite customer experience.

Own Brand Creative Across All Channels

  • Maintain a consistent creative direction across paid media, website, email, organic content, marketplaces, packaging, and launches.
  • Develop practical brand guidelines that support quality, consistency, and speed.
  • Ensure creative work reflects the brand's positioning, audience, and commercial goals.
  • Raise the overall standard of design, copy, video, photography, and storytelling.
  • Protect brand consistency while encouraging experimentation.

Build and Lead a High-Performing Creative Team

  • Lead and develop designers, editors, creators, copywriters, freelancers, and agencies.
  • Set clear responsibilities, quality standards, workflows, and performance expectations.
  • Provide constructive feedback and support team development.
  • Manage the balance between internal and external creative resources.
  • Build a culture of accountability, speed, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Improve Creative Operations and Output

  • Build an efficient process from research and briefing through production, approval, launch, and iteration.
  • Establish clear systems for priorities, deadlines, feedback, approvals, and asset management.
  • Ensure projects are delivered on time and aligned with business priorities.
  • Maintain an organised creative asset library.
  • Improve output and efficiency while maintaining quality and brand consistency.
  • Manage creative budgets and external resources effectively.

Lead Product Launch and Campaign Creative

  • Develop creative strategies for product launches, promotions, seasonal campaigns, and major events.
  • Translate product positioning into strong customer-facing concepts.
  • Define clear messaging, creative direction, asset requirements, and channel execution.
  • Coordinate creative production across paid media, website, email, marketplaces, and organic content.
  • Review results and apply learnings to future campaigns.

Responsibilities

  • Own the overall creative vision and execution across the ecommerce business.
  • Translate company goals into clear creative priorities and plans.
  • Develop quarterly and monthly creative roadmaps.
  • Lead creative concept development and campaign planning.
  • Review and approve high-priority creative assets.
  • Create clear, actionable briefs for internal and external creative teams.
  • Partner with growth, marketing, ecommerce, product, customer service, and leadership teams.
  • Analyse creative performance using advertising, website, email, and marketplace data.
  • Monitor customer behaviour, category trends, competitors, and emerging creative formats.
  • Present creative strategies, results, challenges, and recommendations to senior leadership.
  • Ensure the creative team remains focused on work that has the greatest commercial impact.

Key Performance Indicators

  • Website and landing-page conversion rate.
  • Product-page conversion rate.
  • Advertising creative performance.
  • Customer acquisition cost.
  • Return on advertising spend.
  • Click-through rate and hook rate.
  • Creative testing volume and testing velocity.
  • Percentage of creative tests producing meaningful improvements.
  • Revenue generated from new creative concepts.
  • Email engagement and conversion performance.
  • On-time completion of creative projects.
  • Creative production efficiency.
  • Brand consistency and quality across channels.
  • Performance and development of the creative team.

Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is both creatively ambitious and commercially disciplined. They understand that ecommerce creative must capture attention, communicate value quickly, address customer objections, and motivate action.

They are comfortable moving between high-level strategy and detailed execution. They can confidently lead a team, evaluate creative work, interpret performance data, and collaborate with commercial stakeholders.

They do not rely solely on personal taste. They use customer insight, brand strategy, testing, and business results to make decisions.

Required Experience

  • Significant experience in a senior creative leadership role within ecommerce, DTC, retail, consumer products, or a performance-focused agency.
  • Demonstrated experience improving conversion and advertising performance through creative strategy.
  • Strong understanding of ecommerce customer journeys, product pages, landing pages, paid social, email, and organic content.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary creative teams.
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating both brand-building and performance-focused creative work.
  • Experience creating and evaluating direct-response advertising concepts.
  • Ability to interpret creative, advertising, and ecommerce performance data.
  • Strong understanding of design, copywriting, video, photography, content production, and visual storytelling.
  • Experience managing multiple projects, deadlines, stakeholders, and production partners.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and feedback skills.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience working with physical consumer products.
  • Experience with Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Amazon, Shopify, and email marketing platforms.
  • Experience with conversion-rate optimisation and structured experimentation.
  • Experience producing user-generated content, creator-led advertising, product demonstrations, and testimonial creative.
  • Experience managing external agencies, freelancers, studios, photographers, and creators.
  • Familiarity with creative analytics and project-management tools.
  • Experience scaling an established ecommerce brand across multiple products, markets, or countries.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 90 days, the Creative Director will have assessed the current brand, creative team, workflows, performance data, customer journey, and existing asset library. They will have identified the largest creative and conversion opportunities and introduced a clear testing and production roadmap.

Within six months, the company should have a stronger creative pipeline, clearer brand direction, faster testing cycles, improved collaboration between creative and growth teams, and measurable improvements in conversion and creative performance.

Within the first year, the Creative Director will have built a scalable creative function that consistently produces high-quality, commercially effective work across every major ecommerce channel.

What We Offer:

  • Full-time remote position in a rapidly growing international company.
  • A senior leadership role with direct ownership of the company's ecommerce creative direction and growth.
  • High level of autonomy and the opportunity to shape creative strategy, processes, and team development.
  • Direct impact on ecommerce performance, conversion, and creative effectiveness across multiple channels.
  • Opportunity to build and lead a high-performing multidisciplinary creative team.
  • A performance-driven and feedback-oriented culture where creative decisions are connected to business results.
  • Competitive compensation based on experience.
  • Bonuses.
  • Paid Time Off.
  • Long-term growth opportunities aligned with company expansion.

This is an excellent opportunity for a commercially minded Creative Director who wants to take ownership of a growing ecommerce creative function, combine creative leadership with performance-driven decision-making, and build a scalable creative operation with a direct impact on business growth.

jobs.description:
Client Partner (CP): Role Charter and Job Description

1. ROLE SUMMARY

The Client Partner (CP) owns the commercial performance and strategic relationship for a portfolio of WFX customers. CPs are accountable for renewal execution and expansion growth by leading outcome-based customer conversations and orchestrating internal resources (CSM, Advisory/Pre-Sales, Delivery Owner, Deal Desk). The CP is the quarterback of the account team and ensures the right specialists engage at the right time with a single, consistent customer narrative.

2. WHY THE ROLE EXISTS

WFX is building a GTM model that scales through segmentation, pod-based coverage for Strategic accounts, standardized commercial workflows, and empowered delivery. The CP exists to:

  • Drive profitable retention + growth (GRR/NRR) in the installed base
  • Build executive relationships that reduce churn risk and increase strategic relevance
  • Create and close expansion opportunities using a repeatable playbook
  • Protect time for selling by moving “paper” and operational work to the right functions
  • Ensure delivery commitments and commercial commitments remain aligned

3. PRIMARY OUTCOMES (WHAT “SUCCESS” MEANS)

  1. Renewals closed on timewith minimal surprises and controlled concessions
  2. Expansion growthdriven by account planning and repeatable plays
  3. Executive-level trustand multi-threading across key stakeholders
  4. Forecast integrity(renewal + expansion) leadership can rely on
  5. Internal orchestrationthat reduces friction and accelerates customer decisions

4. SCOPE AND COVERAGE MODEL

CPs own a customer portfolio aligned to WFX segmentation tiers (A1/A2/B1/B2), with coverage intensity based on tier.

4.1. Coverage intent by tier

Segment

CP focus

Coverage posture

A1

Deep strategic coverage, exec governance, multi-threaded expansion

Pod-led, high intensity

A2

Retain and selectively expand, strong governance with lighter intensity

Pod-led, moderate intensity

B1

Create expansion pipeline, prioritize accounts with clear upside

Scaled coverage + targeted specialists

B2

Retain efficiently, low-touch motions, exceptions only

Tech-touch / pooled support

5. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

5.1. Customer strategy and executive relationships

  • Own the account plan (A1/A2 required, B1 simplified) tied to customer outcomes and WFX growth priorities
  • Build and maintain executive sponsor maps and relationship strategies
  • Lead QBR/EBRs for Strategic accounts, ensuring each produces clear next actions and measurable value narratives
  • Serve as the primary commercial escalation point for executive-level issues and risk

5.2. Renewal ownership and retention execution

  • Own renewal outcomes end-to-end: strategy, negotiation approach, internal alignment, and signature
  • Drive renewal discipline using a renewal runway approach (120/90/60/30 milestones) in partnership with CSM and Deal Desk
  • Coordinate approvals and exceptions through defined governance paths
  • Protect profitability by aligning renewals to pricing/margin guardrails and approved exception processes

5.3. Expansion and growth

  • Build and advance expansion pipeline through account-based discovery, targeted plays, and multi-stakeholder alignment
  • Own commercial close on expansions, including bundled solutions across services, managed services, AI, and ecosystem capabilities
  • Keep the solution narrative anchored on measurable outcomes and value realization
  • Partner with Advisory/Pre-Sales and Delivery Owner to translate customer needs into feasible, scoped outcomes

5.4. Orchestration and operating cadence

  • Lead the internal pod rhythm for Strategic accounts (cadence appropriate to tier and complexity)
  • Ensure role clarity across CSM, Advisory/Pre-Sales, Delivery Owner, and Deal Desk to prevent work leakage
  • Maintain CRM hygiene and forecast accuracy for renewals and expansions
  • Capture key account intelligence and stakeholder context in the system of record

6. DECISION RIGHTS (MUST BE ENFORCED)

  • Owns the final recommendation on commercial strategy for renewals and expansions
  • Can commit to delivery-related milestones only when Delivery Owner confirms feasibility and scope assumptions
  • Can request pricing structures and quote development via Deal Desk within standard guardrails
  • Escalates margin exceptions, non-standard terms, and high-risk commitments via defined approval paths

7. EXPLICIT EXCLUSIONS (TO PREVENT ROLE DRIFT)

The CP does not:

  • Generate quotes, renewal paperwork, approvals packets, or contract administration (Deal Desk owns)
  • Own invoicing mechanics, usage reconciliation, or credit execution (Finance/Order Ops owns)
  • Serve as the support engineer or ticket owner (Support/TAM lane; CSM orchestrates)
  • Run delivery project management (Delivery Owner leads delivery governance)
  • Own solution architecture (Advisory/Pre-Sales leads; CP owns the commercial narrative)

8. KEY INTERFACES (HOW CP WORKS WITH THE REST OF THE MODEL)

  • CSM:adoption/value realization, health and risk sensing, governance cadence, renewal runway discipline
  • Advisory/Pre-Sales (Client Advisor):discovery, solutioning, demos, technical validation, roadmap shaping
  • Advisory Services:productized advisory engagements that create roadmaps and unlock expansions
  • Delivery Owner:delivery outcomes, costing inputs, change control triggers, scope feasibility
  • Deal Desk:pricing structure support, quote/renewal paper, approvals routing, guardrails enforcement
  • Finance/Order Ops:billing readiness, delinquency awareness, credits/usage workflows (as defined)

9. REQUIRED ARTIFACTS AND “DEFINITION OF DONE”

A CP is expected to maintain and use the following artifacts (tier-scaled):

  • Account plan and 90-day play plan
  • Stakeholder map and executive sponsor plan
  • Renewal runway plan (120/90/60/30 milestones and escalation triggers)
  • Mutual action plan for material expansions
  • QBR/EBR agenda and value scorecard narrative (A tiers)
  • Internal pod summary notes following key meetings, with next actions and owners

10. PERFORMANCE MEASURES (KPIS)

10.1. Core KPIs

  • Portfolio GRR and NRR
  • Renewals on-time rateand renewal forecast accuracy
  • Expansion pipeline coverageand progression velocity
  • Expansion win rate and average discount behavior vs guardrails
  • Executive engagement coverage for Strategic accounts (documented sponsor + cadence)

10.2. Quality KPIs

  • Margin compliance and exception discipline
  • Low “surprise churn” rate (risks surfaced early with action plans)
  • Adoption of standard plays and artifacts (process adherence tied to outcomes)

11. QUALIFICATIONS AND CAPABILITIES

  • Demonstrated success managing and growing complex customer portfolios (enterprise or upper mid-market)
  • Strong executive presence, negotiation skills, and multi-stakeholder deal leadership
  • Comfort selling blended solutions: advisory, implementation, managed services, AI-enabled CX improvement
  • High operational rigor (forecasting, CRM discipline, play execution)
  • Ability to lead cross-functional teams without formal authority

jobs.description:
CEO Advisor | SMB Leadership Experience Required | $182K+ Earning Potential | Remote

How To MANAGE a Small Law Firm (HTM)

You've built and grown businesses, made the tough decisions, and owned the results. Now put that experience to work helping other business owners do the same.

Compensation: $110,000 base salary + uncapped performance-based compensation, with the opportunity to earn $182,000+ annually.

Location: 100% remote. Candidates must reside in AZ, CO, FL, GA, ID, IL, LA, MD, MI, MO, NC, NE, NJ, NY, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, VA, WA, WV. Due to state registration requirements, we can only employ candidates in these states.

The Opportunity

What if you could use your experience as a CEO to make a meaningful impact across multiple small and midsized businesses instead of running just one?

As a CEO Advisor, you'll work directly with small law firm owners, typically running businesses with $1M–$5M in annual revenue. You'll help them improve profitability, strengthen operations, solve business challenges, and grow.

We're looking for someone who has actually operated and scaled a small or midsized business as its CEO. You understand the realities of running a business without layers of management or unlimited resources. You've owned the P&L, made tough decisions, and been accountable for results.

This is a hands-on advisory role. You'll help owners identify what's holding them back, develop practical solutions, and follow through until results improve.

HTM provides client acquisition and business development support, so you can focus on advising clients rather than finding them.

What You'll Do

  • Drive growth and profitability: Help owners identify opportunities and improve pricing, margins, cash flow, and financial performance.
  • Solve business problems: Identify operational challenges and implement practical solutions.
  • Create accountability: Challenge assumptions, establish priorities, and help owners follow through on their plans.
  • Build stronger businesses: Develop the systems and processes needed for sustainable growth.

What You Must Bring

  • SMB operating experience: Significant experience leading small to midsized businesses, ideally with annual revenues between $500K and $30M.
  • Actual CEO experience: At least eight years of hands-on business leadership, including serving as the actual operating CEO with full P&L responsibility.
  • Proven growth: Personally, led a business through meaningful revenue growth, ideally from approximately $500K to $10M+.
  • Company-wide accountability: Responsible for overall financial and operational performance, not just a department or function.
  • Owner-facing leadership: Comfortable working directly with business owners, challenging assumptions, coaching through difficult decisions, and creating accountability.
  • Hands-on execution: You don't just recommend solutions. You help implement them.

Important: You do not need to have owned the company you scaled. However, you must have served as its actual operating CEO and personally led its growth. Consulting, coaching, advising, fractional executive, or department leadership experience does not substitute for this requirement.

Be prepared to identify the company you led, its annual revenue when you took over and when you left, your P&L responsibilities, and the decisions you personally made to drive growth. We are looking for actual company revenue, not pipeline, valuation, capital raised, or revenue you influenced as an advisor.

This Role Is Not for You If…

  • Your experience is primarily with large enterprises, and you haven't worked directly with small or midsized businesses.
  • You've never served as the actual operating CEO with full P&L responsibility.
  • Your experience is primarily consulting, coaching, advising, or fractional executive work.
  • You've managed a department or prefer strategy without hands-on execution.
  • You're looking for a side gig. This is a full-time commitment.

Compensation & Benefits

  • $110,000 guaranteed base salary.
  • Uncapped performance-based compensation, with the opportunity to earn $182,000+ annually.
  • Full-time W-2 employment.
  • 100% remote within the eligible states listed above.
  • Benefits package and unlimited PTO.

Why HTM?

How To MANAGE a Small Law Firm helps attorneys build stronger businesses behind their legal practices. As a CEO Advisor, you'll bring your real-world operating experience to owners who need help with profitability, cash flow, hiring, operations, and growth.

Ready to Make an Impact?

Apply with your resume and make your operating track record clear. Tell us which company you led, its annual revenue when you took over and when you left, and how you helped drive its growth.

We're looking for someone who has actually run a small or midsized business — and can help other business owners do the same.

Salary: $110,000 – $182,000 / year

We're a team of builders, problem-solvers, and public sector champions. We've built a workplace around a straightforward idea: people do their best work when they're trusted, supported, and not running on empty.

Here's what that actually looks like:

🏢 How we work

We're hybrid — three days a week in our Oakville or Atlanta offices, with standard hours on those days. What the remaining days look like depends on your role and your manager. We talk about it early in the process so there are no surprises on either side.

Twice a year, you get an extra day tacked onto a long weekend. We think recharging is part of doing good work — not a reward for it. Use it however you need.

🙌 Community is part of who we are

Our Engagement Committee finds meaningful ways to give back through time, donations, and shared expertise. We're invested in the places where our people actually live and work.

🤝 Philanthropy Time

We give every employee up to eight hours a year to spend on causes that matter to them. We want you to show up for your community — and we make time for it.

🎉 Real connection at scale

You won't know all 600+ people — and that's okay. What matters is building real relationships with the people you work with every day. Our culture team creates consistent opportunities for that, so work doesn't feel isolating.

📈 Room to grow

Whether you're going deep on AI, building expertise in government tech, or stepping into a bigger role, we invest in your development — through budget, mentorship, and real opportunity to move when you're ready.

Euna Solutions® is the leading provider of purpose-built, cloud-based software designed to streamline procurement, budgeting, payments, and grants management for public sector and government organizations. Euna's AI-powered features and intelligent automation help organizations make better-informed decisions, ensure compliance, empower collaboration, and reduce administrative burden. Euna's full-cycle financial suite supports more than 3,600 organizations across North America in building trust, enabling transparency, and driving positive community impact. Recognized on Government Technology's GovTech 100 list, Euna Solutions is committed to advancing public sector innovation. To learn more, visit . Euna's privacy policy is available here.

jobs.description:
about us: battleface is building a humanity-focused travel insurance company to bring people and the world together. For too long, travel insurance has centered on the company and not the traveler. We’re changing that by connecting people with customized coverage at the right price, exactly when and where they need it.

Our global assistance arm, Robin Assist, powers the 24/7 support, medical coordination, and claims services that travelers rely on — not just for battleface, but across the industry. Together, we’re setting new standards for how travelers are cared for worldwide.

about the role: we're looking for a Payments & Recovery Specialist to manage international medical provider payments, investigate questionable invoices, negotiate medical bills, and pursue recovery and subrogation opportunities on behalf of our insurance partners.

This is not a traditional accounts payable position. We're looking for someone who can investigate, negotiate, challenge costs, and take ownership of complex cases involving hospitals, medical providers, insurers, legal representatives, and third-party administrators around the world.

You'll work closely with our Medical Assistance, Claims, Finance, and Fraud teams to ensure invoices are legitimate, charges are reasonable, payments are accurate, and recovery opportunities are pursued.

The right person is analytical, commercially minded, detail-oriented, and comfortable challenging providers when something doesn't add up. You'll need to be confident communicating with international hospitals, negotiating settlements, investigating potential fraud, and managing cases through to resolution.

what you'll do:

Medical Provider Payments & Invoice Management

  • Review and validate medical invoices from hospitals, clinics, physicians, and other healthcare providers worldwide.
  • Verify patient details, treatment dates, medical services, invoice accuracy, and supporting documentation.
  • Review medical charges for reasonableness, identify duplicate billing, inflated costs, unnecessary services, and billing discrepancies.
  • Negotiate medical bills, discounts, and full-and-final settlements with international providers.
  • Coordinate payments with Finance, ensuring invoices are approved, properly documented, and paid within agreed timelines.
  • Verify international banking instructions, beneficiary details, SWIFT/IBAN information, and payment requirements before releasing payments.
  • Maintain accurate payment records, track outstanding invoices, and resolve provider payment disputes.
  • Ensure applicable deductibles, patient responsibilities, and agreed discounts are correctly applied.

Cost Containment & Provider Negotiations

  • Research local medical pricing and benchmark charges against reasonable and customary costs.
  • Negotiate directly with hospitals, medical networks, and billing intermediaries to reduce medical expenses.
  • Review high-value medical invoices and challenge questionable treatment costs, procedures, and lengths of stay.
  • Identify opportunities to improve provider payment terms and negotiate better commercial arrangements.
  • Track negotiated savings and report cost containment results to management and insurance partners.
  • Escalate unusual billing patterns, excessive charges, or suspected provider misconduct.

Recovery & Subrogation

  • Identify opportunities to recover medical and claims expenses from responsible third parties, insurers, and other sources.
  • Investigate liability involving accidents, hotels, transportation providers, medical facilities, and other third parties.
  • Coordinate recovery efforts with liability insurers, legal representatives, and international claims organizations.
  • Review accident reports, police documentation, insurance policies, medical records, and other evidence supporting recovery.
  • Pursue coordination of benefits and recoveries from primary or overlapping insurance coverage.
  • Prepare recovery demands, negotiate settlements, and track outstanding recovery balances.
  • Work with external legal counsel when formal recovery or litigation is required.
  • Maintain accurate subrogation records and report recovery results to insurance partners.

Fraud Prevention & Invoice Verification

  • Investigate potentially fraudulent medical invoices, fabricated documentation, and suspicious payment requests.
  • Independently verify hospital legitimacy, provider credentials, patient admissions, and medical billing information.
  • Identify suspicious patterns involving repeat admissions, inflated treatment charges, altered invoices, and unusual payment arrangements.
  • Conduct provider due diligence using independent sources, official records, and direct hospital verification.
  • Collaborate with our Fraud and Claims teams to investigate suspicious claims and recommend appropriate action.
  • Document investigation findings and maintain clear evidence supporting payment or recovery decisions.

Reporting & Operational Improvement

  • Maintain accurate records of payments, negotiations, recoveries, and investigations in our claims management systems.
  • Monitor outstanding payment obligations, recovery opportunities, and overdue cases.
  • Prepare regular reporting on payment volumes, negotiated savings, recovery performance, and suspected fraud.
  • Identify process improvements and opportunities to automate invoice review, verification, and payment workflows.
  • Support the development of internal procedures for international provider payments, cost containment, and subrogation.

what we're looking for:

  • 3+ years of experience in travel insurance, medical assistance, claims administration, healthcare billing, cost containment, or insurance recoveries.
  • Experience reviewing and negotiating medical invoices, ideally involving international healthcare providers.
  • Understanding of insurance claims, medical billing, subrogation, and coordination of benefits.
  • Strong negotiation skills and confidence challenging unreasonable charges and resolving disputes.
  • Familiarity with international payments, banking verification, and cross-border transactions.
  • Ability to review medical documentation, financial records, and insurance policies.
  • Strong investigative and analytical skills with excellent attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Comfortable working independently and managing multiple complex cases simultaneously.
  • Proficiency with claims management systems, spreadsheets, and digital collaboration tools.
  • Willingness to work across international time zones and communicate with providers worldwide.

nice to have:

  • Experience working for a travel insurance company, third-party administrator (TPA), medical assistance company, or international medical cost containment organization.
  • Previous responsibility for medical bill negotiation, provider fraud investigations, or subrogation recoveries.
  • Familiarity with international healthcare systems and medical pricing.
  • Experience working with external legal counsel and liability insurers.
  • Additional languages, particularly Spanish, French, or Portuguese.
  • Experience using AI tools, document analysis, and automated verification systems.

what success looks like:

  • Medical invoices are reviewed, verified, and processed accurately and on time.
  • Unreasonable medical charges are challenged and negotiated before payment.
  • Provider relationships are maintained while protecting our insurance partners from unnecessary costs.
  • Recovery and subrogation opportunities are identified early and actively pursued.
  • Suspicious invoices and fraudulent payment requests are identified before funds are released.
  • Payment backlogs are minimized, and every outstanding case has a clear next action.
  • Measurable savings and recoveries are delivered to our insurance partners.

why join us:

  • You'll be joining a fast-growing international insurance and assistance business where your work has a direct financial and operational impact.
  • You'll have the opportunity to take ownership of complex international cases, negotiate with providers around the world, develop recovery strategies, and help build smarter, technology-driven payment and fraud prevention processes.
  • We're looking for someone who takes initiative, solves problems, and doesn't need to be told what to do next. If you enjoy investigating complex cases, negotiating solutions, and finding ways to make insurance operations more effective, we'd like to hear from you.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Manager – Strategic Partner Sales
jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityRackspace Technology has a strategic partnership with one of the world’s largest enterprise go to market partners.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Rackspace Technology has a strategic partnership with one of the world’s largest enterprise go to market partners. Through it, our cloud services & AI solutions are sold to that partner’s enterprise customer base by the partner’s own sales organisation. This is a rare chance to build a new route to market at scale.

As Enterprise Account Manager, you will be the face of Rackspace inside the partner’s sales organisation. You won’t be working a named list of end customers. Your customer is the partner’s sellers, and your job is to make sure Rackspace is the first name they think of when a client needs cloud, data, security or AI. You’ll build relationships across their account teams, equip them to position us with confidence, and get Rackspace pulled into the right customer opportunities early.


What you will do

Build and grow relationships across the partner’s sales organisation

  • Establish yourself as a trusted, visible figure with the partner’s sellers, account directors, sales leaders and specialists across industries and regions.
  • Run a structured engagement plan: regular account reviews, one-to-ones, team meetings and joint events, so Rackspace stays front of mind.
  • Gain access to the partner’s wider sales community, and open doors for Rackspace’s own executives and technical teams.

Drive pipeline through the partner

  • Identify the partner accounts and opportunities where Rackspace’s cloud, managed services, data, security and AI offerings add value, and shape joint opportunity plans around them.
  • Get Rackspace pulled into customer deals at the right stage, working alongside partner sellers from first conversation through to close.
  • Take ownership of opportunity registration, qualification and pipeline progression, keeping forecasts accurate and visible.
  • Work with partner sellers and Rackspace Solutions Architects on discovery, solution design and proposals, including RFI and RFP responses and commercial negotiation.

Enable and promote

  • Educate and inspire the partner’s sellers on the full Rackspace portfolio, including our AI solutions and compute, through briefings, workshops, use-case stories and joint customer wins.
  • Create simple, credible messaging that makes it easy for a seller who isn’t a Rackspace product portfollio specialist to spot an opportunity and bring us in.
  • Partner with Rackspace marketing on joint campaigns, events, case studies and customer references.

Own the partnership commercially

  • Build and run a joint business plan, with clear targets, priorities and cadence, and report on progress to Rackspace leadership and the partner.
  • Understand how the partner’s sellers are measured and rewarded and use that to make selling Rackspace the easy choice for them.
  • Act as the voice of the partner inside Rackspace, bringing back feedback to product, pre-sales, legal and commercial teams, and resolving issues quickly.

What you will bring

Essential

  • Proven track record of selling technology services through a large partner, systems integrator, carrier, distributor or alliance, or of selling alongside a partner’s sales team in a co-sell model.
  • A sales-focused account management background, with a history of meeting or exceeding quota in enterprise IT, cloud, managed services or a comparable sector.
  • Outstanding networking and relationship-building skills. You are comfortable earning credibility with people you don’t manage and who have no obligation to sell for you.
  • Ability to influence without authority, from frontline sellers to senior leaders.
  • Strong commercial acumen: you can qualify, structure and negotiate complex, multi-party deals, and handle RFIs and RFPs.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, in writing and in person.
  • Self-starter who is organised enough to manage a broad network and a long-cycle pipeline, while still delivering in-year numbers.

Desirable

  • Knowledge of the cloud landscape (public, private and hybrid cloud, managed services, FinOps and migration), and an appetite for AI, data and compute.
  • Experience in regulated or public sector markets, or with sovereignty and data-residency requirements.
  • Familiarity with partner programmes, deal registration, joint business planning and partner-led marketing.
  • CRM experience (we use [Salesforce]) and disciplined pipeline management.
  • Professional sales training and a recognised sales methodology.

What success looks like

First 90 days: You’ve met and built early relationships with the key partner sellers and leaders, and you understand how the partner sells, is organised and is rewarded. You have a joint plan agreed and your first opportunities in the pipeline.

First year: Rackspace is a known, trusted name across the partner’s sales force. You have a healthy, partner-influenced and partner-sourced pipeline, repeatable enablement and a growing list of joint wins. You will have built strong relationships with our partners GTM sellers and fully positioned Rackspace’s capabilities with that community.


Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several geographic markets. The compensation range for this position ranges from £138,226.00/year in our lowest geographic market up to £221,038.00/year in our highest geographic market. Pay is based on a number of factors including market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process. The compensation package may also include incentive compensation opportunities in the form of annual bonus or incentives, equity awards and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP). Learn more about benefits at Rackspace.

About Rackspace Technology

Rackspace Technology is the trusted operator of the full enterprise AI stack, from governed private cloud to AI inference and agents in production. From edge to core to cloud, we operate the infrastructure, data layer, and software integration to deliver business outcomes with the predictable cost, reliability, security, and compliance that regulated and mission-critical environments demand. We support customers in more than 120 countries with AI capabilities spanning private cloud, public cloud, applications, data and cyber resilience.


More on Rackspace Technology

Though we’re all different, Rackers thrive through our connection to a central goal: to be a valued member of a winning team on an inspiring mission. We bring our whole selves to work every day. And we embrace the notion that unique perspectives fuel innovation and enable us to best serve our customers and communities around the globe. We welcome you to apply today and want you to know that we are committed to offering equal employment opportunity without regard to age, color, disability, gender reassignment or identity or expression, genetic information, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity status, military or veteran status, nationality, ethnic or national origin, race, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any legally protected characteristic. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

jobs.title: Ingénieur Senior en sécurité réseau F5 (Freelance possible)
jobs.excerpt: 📋 Tâches et responsabilitésPrésentationVous prenez en charge l’infrastructure F5 et l’Advanced Web Application Firewall (AWAF), avec pour objectif de sécuriser les applications et les environnements informatiques.
jobs.description:
📋 Tâches et responsabilités

Présentation

Vous prenez en charge l’infrastructure F5 et l’Advanced Web Application Firewall (AWAF), avec pour objectif de sécuriser les applications et les environnements informatiques. Vous contribuez à la digitalisation et à la modernisation des systèmes, tout en assurant une veille continue de leur niveau de sécurité et une intervention rapide en situation de crise.

📌 Mission

La fonction couvre la gestion, la sécurisation et l’évolution de l’infrastructure F5/AWAF. Elle comprend également le suivi et l’évaluation continus de la sécurité des systèmes informatiques, ainsi que la gestion des incidents tels que les attaques organisées, les intrusions réseau et la détection de virus.

Livrables

  • Infrastructure F5/Advanced Web Application Firewall installée, configurée et administrée
  • Politiques de sécurité élaborées, documentées et suivies
  • Analyses de risques techniques réalisées sur les différents systèmes informatiques
  • Solutions mises en œuvre pour remédier aux vulnérabilités identifiées
  • Recommandations concernant la sécurisation technique des connexions avec les partenaires via l’intranet et Internet
  • Documentation technique et rapports d’incident ou de crise

Tâches principales

  • Administrer l’infrastructure de sécurité F5 et l’Advanced Web Application Firewall
  • Installer, configurer et gérer F5 AWAF
  • Développer et documenter les politiques de sécurité, puis suivre leur application
  • Surveiller et évaluer en continu le niveau de sécurité des systèmes informatiques et leur protection contre les actions malveillantes
  • Intervenir efficacement lors de situations de crise, notamment en cas d’attaques organisées, d’intrusions réseau ou de détection de virus
  • Conseiller les équipes sur les solutions techniques permettant de sécuriser les connexions avec les partenaires externes via l’intranet et Internet
  • Réaliser des analyses de risques techniques à des fins de gestion
  • Mettre en œuvre les mesures nécessaires pour remédier aux vulnérabilités identifiées

Compétences clés

  • Installation, configuration et administration de l’infrastructure F5 AWAF, notamment APM, ASM, LTM, Identity Provider et SSL VPN
  • Surveillance et évaluation continues de la sécurité des systèmes, ainsi que gestion des crises liées aux attaques, intrusions et virus
  • Analyse des risques techniques et remédiation des vulnérabilités
  • Maîtrise des routeurs, des firewalls stateful packet inspection et des firewalls applicatifs, notamment Palo Alto, Forcepoint et Panorama
  • Maîtrise des solutions VPN, remote access et site-to-site, des web proxies et des solutions terminal-serveur telles que Citrix
  • Utilisation d’outils de monitoring et de corrélation des logs, notamment Splunk, Nessus et Elastic SIEM
  • Bonne connaissance des protocoles TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, SSL et SNMP
  • Connaissance de la sécurisation des réseaux sans fil, notamment WiFi, WEP, WPA et WPA2, ainsi que des principes de chiffrement à clé publique et à clé privée
  • Documentation rigoureuse et communication claire avec les équipes et le management

Communication et collaboration

  • Très bonnes capacités de communication écrite et orale, avec aptitude à documenter clairement le travail réalisé dans des rapports et documents techniques
  • Capacité à travailler en équipe avec une approche méthodique, précise et orientée vers les besoins du rôle
  • Le bilinguisme français-néerlandais est privilégié. Une connaissance de base suffisante de l’autre langue nationale peut également convenir. L’anglais technique est indispensable.

Niveau et expérience

  • Profil technique senior, capable de travailler de manière autonome sous supervision générale, conformément au niveau 4 « Enable » de SFIA
  • Minimum 10 ans d’expérience en sécurité informatique
  • Autonomie, sens de l’initiative et capacité à intervenir efficacement en situation de crise. Il ne s’agit pas d’un poste junior.

Diplôme

Diplôme de gradué ou de licencié en informatique ou en électronique, ou expérience confirmée équivalente.

En pratique

Niveau de responsabilité : SFIA niveau 4 « Enable », profil technique senior
Rapporte à : Responsable de l’équipe réseau et sécurité
Régime de travail : Temps plein, télétravail possible
Lieu de travail : Bruxelles
Collaboration : Équipes systèmes, opérations et projets

📝 Votre profil

Expérience

Une expérience en tant qu’Expert Network Engineer est attendue.

Compétences techniques

  • Firewalls et filtrage : routeurs, firewalls stateful packet inspection et firewalls applicatifs, notamment Palo Alto
  • Outils de monitoring et de corrélation des logs : Splunk, Nessus et Elastic SIEM
  • Protocoles et sécurité réseau : TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, SSL et SNMP
  • Sécurisation des réseaux sans fil : WiFi, WEP, WPA et WPA2, ainsi que principes de chiffrement à clé publique et à clé privée
  • Solutions VPN remote access et site-to-site, web proxy et solutions terminal-serveur telles que Citrix

Langues

  • Néerlandais
  • Anglais technique
  • Français

💼 Offre

Vous ferez partie d'une PME belge en pleine croissance, où l’initiative et le développement personnel sont encouragés. Nous vous offrirons un environnement de travail agréable, entouré(e) de collègues sympathiques. Ensemble, nous élaborerons un plan de carrière, avec une attention particulière et un budget dédié à la formation ou à la certification complémentaire. Vous pouvez compter sur un salaire attractif, complété par des avantages extra-légaux, y compris une voiture de société.

Audit & Compliance

Reporting & Analytics

Collaboration & Communication
